content.rationale: S3-divergence fixes the verdict and its source — the commits the revset `divergent()` yields, over a spawned jj process; M-layout places the module flat at src/divergence.rs. It crosses `jj log --ignore-working-copy --no-graph -r divergent() -T commit_id` and answers whether the set is non-empty, carrying failures as values with their evidence (S3-err); the read is observational (S5-observation, urqytyqn), so it never snapshots the state it is judging. A revert can rewrite a commit below the working copy as readily as the working copy itself, so the verdict is not scoped to `@`. Nothing here reverts or refuses: taking the verdict and rolling back belongs to the undo and redo verbs (S5-revert-divergent, ppytsptl).
